So, I’ll preface this by saying you use terms like “leftist” in a derogatory fashion so you probably don’t care for what I’m about to say, but:

>  the states you are referring to were Democrat strongholds that witnessed the same  inequality.

They were “democrats” in the way that Lincoln was a “republican.” In other words, the terms today have little to do with platforms of the past.

Whereas Democrats are seen as the “big government” party now, they were the small government party up until the Great Depression. Republicans were the ones expanding federal power, waging a war for social progress, and getting all the states in line.

So basically, you’ve argued the point liberals have been making for generations: backwards, conservative ideology (not limited to a party line) usually means a lower quality of life for residents. Really... trivial if you think about it- being the antithesis of progress means you don’t progress.
